desc:
prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i. You may complete at most two transactions. A transaction is one purchase of a single share followed by a sale on a strictly later day. You can hold at most one share at a time, so the first sale must happen before the second purchase (selling and buying again on the same day is allowed).

Return the maximum total profit. If no profitable trade exists, return 0.

Example: prices = [3,3,5,0,0,3,1,4] gives 6: buy at 0 and sell at 3 (profit 3), then buy at 1 and sell at 4 (profit 3).
hints: With one transaction you only need the lowest price so far. With two, the second trade starts from the profit the first one already made.
At any moment you are in one of four situations: bought the first share, sold the first, bought the second, sold the second. Keep the best balance for each.
Per price p: b1 = max(b1, -p), s1 = max(s1, b1 + p), b2 = max(b2, s1 - p), s2 = max(s2, b2 + p). Start with b1 = b2 = -infinity and s1 = s2 = 0; the answer is s2.
editorial: Model the process as a small state machine with four balances. b1 is the best cash while holding the share of the first transaction (price paid is subtracted), s1 the best cash after finishing it, b2 the best cash while holding the share of the second, s2 the best cash after finishing both. Each day can only move forward along that chain or stay put.

Update in the order b1, s1, b2, s2 using the new values of the previous stage. Using today's s1 when computing b2 corresponds to selling and re-buying on the same day, which the statement allows (and which never beats simply holding). Because s1 and s2 start at 0, 'fewer than two transactions' is covered automatically.

One pass with four variables: O(n) time, O(1) space. The same idea extends to k transactions with arrays buy[j] and sell[j]. An alternative is to compute the best single trade ending on or before each day (prefix) and starting on or after each day (suffix) and combine them at the split point.
solution:
def maxProfitTwo(prices):
    b1 = b2 = -10 ** 9
    s1 = s2 = 0
    for p in prices:
        b1 = max(b1, -p)
        s1 = max(s1, b1 + p)
        b2 = max(b2, s1 - p)
        s2 = max(s2, b2 + p)
    return s2
